lesson: build.compare answers on two axes that can disagree, and this is the pair that proves why: identical inputs, identical output bytes, and a build that now fails. The verdict is identical and the transition is broken, both true at once - a single pass/fail score would have to pick one and would hide the other. The interpretation is prose for the verdict rather than for the pair, so it says the bytes matched and says nothing about the exit code, which is the transition’s job. sameReceipt is null rather than false when either side omitted its receipt, because two receipts that were never compared is not the same as two that differed.
